data.body: Landed as Gerrit change 3108, commit 63b75758a3c (LLM-Review +1 with no advisories, Verified +1, 0 unresolved). Reproduced deterministically before any change, without load: a scratch copy of the test whose git shim sleeps before delegating to real git. Healthy-call delay 0 s and 0.2 s: pass. 0.45 s (real git adds the rest, landing just over the 0.5 s per-attempt bound): fails with exactly 'git was invoked 4 times', the reported outcome, while after == before held, so the guard behaved correctly and only the count assertion failed. Root cause: the test stalled 'the second rev-parse HEAD' and asserted a total of 3 invocations; both encode timing, so any healthy probe that exceeds the bound is also retried and shifts the count. Fix: a marker-armed shim stalls exactly one probe and logs stall/ok per probe; the test asserts the contract (one stall, a healthy probe after it, HEAD not reported moved) with a 2 s per-attempt bound. The new test passes with healthy calls delayed 0.45 s and 0.9 s and fails when the guard does not resample (GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS=1); the persistent-stall tests and tests/_isolation.py are unchanged. make verify locally: only the 17 known pandoc failures, no errors; Linux CI green. Not observed: the original single failure itself was never re-seen, so its link to host load is inferred from the delayed-shim reproduction.
